intro: A monitoring dashboard compares populations through fixed bins. Smoothing keeps empty bins finite, but its size changes the reported population stability index.
task: Calculate smoothed distribution-shift contributions and inspect how empty bins and differing sample totals affect the result.
requirements: reference_counts and current_counts are equal-length nonempty vectors of integer-valued counts in [0,1000000], each with positive total. smoothing is a real scalar in [1e-12,1e30].
Add smoothing to every count, normalize each population independently, and calculate contributions (q-p)*log(q/p).
Return dict reference and current as probability vectors, contributions as a vector, and psi as their sum. Bin boundaries must already be aligned by the caller.

Numeric inputs must be real and finite with magnitude at most 1e30, except where a stricter bound is stated. Booleans are not numeric parameters. Leave all caller inputs unchanged and raise ValueError for invalid inputs.

hints.title: Normalize separately
hints.body: Reference and current populations may have different total sizes.

hints.title: Compute in both directions
hints.body: The product of probability difference and log ratio is unchanged when the populations are swapped.

explanation: The PSI compares two discrete distributions on shared bins. A positive pseudocount prevents division by zero, and every contribution is nonnegative because its two factors have matching signs.
Results depend on binning and smoothing. The implementation reports the statistic and its contributions without attaching universal severity thresholds.
